claims.claim: The gameplay loop is criticized for heavy pacing issues, consisting primarily of alternating short walking segments, cutscenes, and brief button-mashing fights.

citations.review_text:
I really wanted to enjoy Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade, but it just wasn't for me. The game leans far too heavily into long story sequences and dialogue, leaving me wishing I was actually playing more often. Much of the story didn't hold my interest, and the combat never evolved into anything particularly engaging. It was easy enough that auto-combat handled most encounters, making Materia feel largely unnecessary. Most battles ended so quickly that I rarely had the opportunity to use summons, which made them feel like wasted potential.

The game also includes several design choices that became frustrating over time. Friendly character collision while moving around is surprisingly annoying, and the forced overland tasks felt like uninspired filler rather than meaningful gameplay. While I appreciate the production quality and understand why longtime fans love it and why many purists and fans of the original may hate or were disappointed by it, I came away disappointed. I will try to finish the game and I may edit or change parts of this review.

I've finally realized why a lot of the Final Fantasy games feel so bad to play. In every single one of them, there's always some glaring flaw that either ruins the game or severely hurts the enjoyment for me. Every single one of them has it, whether it's a completely broken port that doesn't run like in FF10, horrendous gameplay in FF15, or a corridor simulator in FF13. It's basically like a test of how much you can stomach. If you can get past all that (or if your game actually works), you'll love these games.

That said, the flaw here is that it doesn't feel like a game; it feels more like an interactive movie or an on-rails game. You will do the following from start to finish: cutscene -> 10-20 seconds of walking -> cutscene -> 20-40 seconds of fighting (mashing 2 buttons) -> cutscene. It basically never lets you sit with it, and when it FINALLY does, you realize it's all just padding. They took a 5-hour opening section and stretched it out to 35~ hours through the worst possible pacing. Cutscene here, walking there, go up a ladder, go down a ladder, open this door except you can't cause it's locked, so find a key, repeat.

I really dislike it when games coddle you like a little child, yelling in your ear about everything. If you're even remotely low, characters will yell at you to heal EVERY time. If you kill an enemy, everyone HAS to speak. If you do anything, Cloud will comment on it with his cringey dialogue. The biggest thing is that, once again, the combat just isn't good. Go back to the turn-based gameplay, PLEASE, cause mashing 2 buttons on a boss and then spamming heal isn't fun. Then you kill it, and it comes back to life and goes longer. Every enemy, even in the opening sequence, feels like a sponge; it just isn't satisfying or entertaining to fight.

The graphics look great, but that's about all I really liked. This one isn't for me. Too mind-numbing too early. If big flashing lights easily entertain you and you giggle and clap when explosions happen,…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from severe pacing issues due to heavy padding, forced filler content, and lengthy segments of slow walking or narrow corridors.

citations.review_text:
What a waste of my time. This game is essentially a slow walking and narrow corridor simulator, to the point it was comically obvious how they're trying so hard to pad the game.

The only good thing about the game is the graphics and the combat system, which admittedly is probably the best FF combat system to date (haven't played Rebirth though). That said, the game is paced so poorly, you will spend most of your time walking slowly, and being forced to move through narrow spaces.

The story is... fine. The dialogue was for the most part Saturday cartoon levels of writing. Nothing to write home about. If you want to see the story, just go to youtube, this was just painful to play through.

The game is also horribly paced. While the combat was good, you will instead spend most of your time just walking slowly, and doing side quests that barely contribute anything to the story or character development.

Sephiroth is cool asf, however, this game is not.

First of all I must say that I never played the original Final Fantasy 7, which I have heard great things about, but I will after playing this horrendous game. Before I bash this game, there a few things it did well. The graphics, absolutely stunning. From the character models to the environment. The world in this game is also so interesting to me.

Now the bad. This game is just a hallway walking simulator where there are an EGREGIOUS amount of sections that slow your movement to a halt because there is a crate you need to squeeze between or a random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ balance beam. Don't even get me started on the amount of times this game just takes away your ability to run for NO REASON. I understand that some games slow down the player's speed in order to make a scene feel more cinematic, but this game decides that taking away your ability to run during a FORCED fetch quest is completely okay and justifiable. The story is this game is also not good at all because of how slow and padded it feels to get anywhere in that story. This game is a remake of just the first EIGHT HOURS of the original that was just stretched to be a full game. Without even knowing that, you can tell. The first 13 chapters of the story (which includes some of the longest chapters in the game) should have been condensed into a half or even a third of the runtime. The reason for that is that those chapters are basically all the earlier described hallway walks with very basic mash X on your controller combat every 30 seconds or so. And don't even get me started on the Whispers which has to be one of the dumbest parts of this game.

This game should have just been a full faithful remake of the original game which I have heard so many better things about.

Game starts out alright but quickly suffers from severe pacing issues and bloat. Combat is fun, albeit with a slight identity crisis, and the lore/story is interesting, but between all of that exists a ton of padding and filler to extend runtime. Nothing encapsulates this more than all the forced interruptions whether it's slow walking sections, traversal mechanics (tightrope, crevice etc) or a million doors with levers that require you to stand there and hold the button down for no reason. 

Should also be noted that PC controls are dreadful. It should not be necessary to rebind 90% of the keys, and then still require mods on top of that, just to create functional controls for kb/m. "Console game designed for controllers" is not a valid excuse

FF7 Remake accurately taps into and transposes the essence of the 1997 Playstation original and brings to life the world we all imagined we were experiencing when we played it 20 years ago. In retaining all the most impactful moments (including cheeky nods to the original's quirky and sometimes bizarre charactarisation) while expanding the game to meet modern technological standards without a single moment of incongruence, this feels almost like a miracle. They've captured a shared but literally intangible experience and elevated it in many ways, and playing FF7 Remake feels like one of the most stark successes of artistic translation I've ever witnessed.

It is true to the original's best and most impactful aspects while new and interesting enough to be worth the money. And while there's no downside to just playing the original, at this point I can almost *almost* say that this feels like a definitive version of FF7 in the modern day. There are a few things that hold it back however: it is bogged down by too much tedious throttling of character movement for the purposes of storytelling, peppered with forgettable filler as journeys that were more or less omitted from the original become 45 minutes of running through linear corridors and fighting group after group of enemies, and (while this is hardly a criticism) people who have never played the original may wish to return and find it impossibly quaint by comparison.

I focus on these aspects specifically, rather than, for example, the masterpiece that is the remake's soundtrack, because I think it's important to understand that both versions of this game have specific merits that the other lacks. One of the reasons the original was so impactful was because of the way it subverted or outright overstepped the traditional limitations of the genre. JRPGs are, on the whole, incredibly derivative, but FF7 excelled and differentiated itself not only in the quality of its story, music, and grand aesthetic vision, but in th…

Go play the original if you want to play a good game and if you played that there is no guarantee that you'll like this one.

They stretched 4 hours of gameplay into an entire game and you can tell. So many sections where you are forced to walk around waiting for dialogue, so much that more the half of what i played so far was cutscenes or walking cutscenes. They stretched every single possible section of the original to pad game time and not with interesting dialogues but literally just small talk in between characters, very annoying when in the original takes a couple of minutes to go from point A to point B and in this game is just walking down a corridor and takes 15 minutes with just the most mundane ♥♥♥♥ like moving a box or just climbing some ladder. Detours consist of walking 5 seconds down a path collecting a chest most of the time. In "dungeons" you might get an extra fight before the reward.
Barely any new content and even that is just a few side quests before continuing the original story for another few chapters. 
Speaking of chapters i find it so weird how short the chapters are and some of them are just a linear story section that connects into another linear story section. Not sure why it bothers me but it feels like just another way to pad something, in this case achievements, since you get one for each chapter. 

My biggest grip is how bad the battle system is. Some bosses can be fun to play but most of the time it just doesn't feel good to play. It's an inbetween a pseudo action game and a turn base. 
Your dodge is just an animation cancel has 0 iframe and can only dodge some melee attacks; almost all range attacks will still hit because they either are homing or aoe. Guard also very mid, as soon as any attack hit from a higher angle it stops working (i guess i have to teleport away to be able to block some attacks). Guard does have a counter but it's not for perfect blocks you just need to be holding the guard button before the melee attack hits.…

It looks good. Midgar is an iconic city and it's never looked better.
The voice acting is mostly very good.
The music is well orchestrated. I like the remixes and the way they're integrated into the world.
It's got a lot of nostalgia for players of FF7, from characters to locales.

Cons:
None of that matters with how poorly optimized the game is on PC. Stuttering cutscenes and skipping audio seem to be a common problem.
Despite being marketed as a "remake" it's a sequel in ways that only make sense if you're familiar with the original.
The pacing is so  s  l  o  w  ,
Despite being iconic, Midgar is an ugly ass city by design.

And if you haven't played the original FF7, good luck understanding why ghosts and Sephiroth from Smash Bros keep showing up randomly.

The bigger issue is how slow everything else is. The pre-rendered backgrounds of the original game served the mood of each room in a specific way but in Remake it mostly turns into hallways in between set pieces and combat arenas. As someone who absolutely loves the original FF7, this is one of those games I desperately wanted to like. I really gave it multiple chances purely because of how much affection I have for the original characters, world and story. And to be fair, technically and visually it is undeniably impressive. The soundtrack is fantastic, the character models look great and some of the cinematic moments genuinely hit hard if you have nostalgia for the original.

But the actual gameplay experience just felt bloated and exhausting to me.

The pacing is genuinely awful. The game constantly interrupts itself every couple of minutes with slow walking sections, forced crawling through gaps, squeezing between walls, automated climbing animations and endless cutscenes where characters explain painfully obvious things. It often feels like you spend more time watching people discuss pressing a button than actually playing the game. A section that took a few hours in the original gets stretched into a 30+ hour experience through pure filler and it really shows.

Combat also never clicked for me. It sits awkwardly between action combat and turn based RPG systems without really committing to either. Basic fights can mostly be won by mashing attack and healing occasionally, while harder fights often boil down to pausing, swapping materia for the enemy weakness and then steamrolling them. Unfortunately cannot recommend this version of game due to endless problems on Linux. The game runs on my notebook in 1080p / 60  fps on high / high. I have tried many settings (even 30 fps / low / low) and different Proton versions with no success. The only difference is time until the cutscene freezes. This happens on Fedora 44, CachyOS and Nixos but not on Windows 11.

Also Xbox controller repeatedly loses button assignment with need to restart the game multiple times to fix this.

I do NOT have such problems in ANY other game i play on Linux, even much newer ones. Don't understand this, as this is a Steam deck / Steam box / Steam OS verified.

citations.review_text: Im recommending it, but only because you will need to play it if you wanna play the others. I grew up on the OG 7 as a kid and love it to death. This game looks pretty sure, but by god its boring. Hallway after hallway, sewer after sewer etc etc. Its just not exciting at all. The level design and share drawn out padding make this game outstay its welcome. Stretching midgar which is a five hour portion into a 30 plus hour game leads to a lot of bloaty boredom. Get it if your a fan, grind it out and then move on to rebirth

This was ultimately not interesting and varied enough to be a standalone experience. There are enjoyable moments but these are far and few between and by the time I got to the final chapters I just wanted it to be over. Levels don't feel like levels but like I'm just stuck in these endless corridors that would make P.T. era Kojima cream his pants. Final Fantasy VII Remake is a masterclass in how to ruin a classic with bloat, artificial friction, and garbage design. The combat system is completely built like trash. It tries to blend action and menus but fails miserably at both, resulting in an over-engineered nightmare. Throughout the entire game, you are constantly fighting terrible camera tracking, input lag, and clunky targeting. Worse, the developers obsessed over heavily scripted boss fights bogged down by invisible shield gimmicks, arbitrary phase shifts, and hidden weaknesses that completely ignore actual tactical skill. It turns what should be an exciting battle into a miserable hostage situation.
Square Enix has fallen so incredibly far from their peak. If you want to remember when this company actually knew how to design a masterpiece with flawless pacing, intuitive mechanics, and a truly brilliant battle system, go play Final Fantasy X. This remake is a bloated, artificial, poorly paced disaster. Save your sanity and avoid it.

• Difficulty curve is slow early on; real challenge arrives late.
• Some characters are locked out for long stretches despite having deep kits.
• Limited weapon variety and no transmog/customization options.
• Status effects could use better in‑game explanations.

[h2]The Not‑So‑Good[/h2]
• Platforming and gimmick sections (motorcycle, crane puzzles) feel like padding.
• DLC dialogue is pretty [spoiler]cringe[/spoiler] compared to the main game.

[hr][/hr]

[b]Overall:[/b]
If you love stylish combat, top‑tier music, and beautiful worldbuilding, this remake delivers. It’s not perfect, but the highs are absolutely worth the journey—especially if you enjoy mastering combat systems.

[b]Final Score: 8.5/10[/b]

This game is great, it really is. However there are a bunch of minor things throughout that more or less detract from the overall experience and make it to where it's not an all time great imo. 

This game is mostly on rails from start to finish with one section near the end that somewhat opens everything up. It being on rails is not a problem at all and is quite nice in the era of everything being an empty open world. 

Pacing was good for the most part (not compared to the original, but we will treat this as its own experience, because it is).

Combat was kinda ehh, but not bad overall, it was somewhat easy, but some fights required you to not just slam your head on the controller. 

Story is great, lots of good expansion into characters within the midgar arc though at a point it almost feels like too much. It certainly feels way more alive and vibrant than it did in the original, which makes sense considering it was a quick part of the original (6 hours ish vs 30 lol).

The progression was kind of ass, the weapon level up system didn't feel overly impactful, by the end I put all of them on automatic. RPG elements wise the only part that was fun to mess with to an extent was materia, but felt nowhere near as impactful as the original game outside of covering weaknesses. 

Music is stellar and overall presentation is great and extremely memorable.

All in all this is a great new way to experience FF7 for both newcomers and previous players.

EDIT: Yuffie intermission was fun, some goofy combat with the synergy. Fun minigame (condor fortress). Ramuh (coolest summon imo). Anything further is a spoiler so just enjoy it, pretty short experience.

Lots of nice additions to the universe were made as well. There are, however, many major changes in the story progression compared to the original FF7, and this will surely anger purists. Can't say I'm a huge fan of all the changes, and I will say the ending felt a bit...I don't know, off-key.

The combat system isn't bad if you like action games, but I felt Materia as a whole in this game were just a bit too weak. Perhaps the fights were just too easy that I never really bothered to learn how to play the game properly, but I felt it was generally more effective to use the character abilities granted to them by their weapons, than to cast any offensive magic (in most cases). That is not to say that the original FF7 didn't have its share of balance issues, but I felt the room for creativity that the Materia system in the original provided, didn't exist here, if perhaps because of the more action-oriented change.

There are lots of complaints of padding, and I do think that is valid. Though many of the side quests are optional, the game does more or less guilt you into doing them. The combat system in this game is not very good, it is quite a bit worse than Nier and older final fantasy games. And it sucks because you often have to wait 30-40 minutes between combat watching incredibly boring cutscenes and walking slowly.

About 5% of the time it feels like you have a reason to use the combat they way it was designed: rotate characters, set up staggers, use ability rotations, and dodge/block. There are a lot of interesting concepts and combos available that could make for really fun combat. But the balance of most encounters and the implementation of some of these elements are really sloppy.

90% of the time, the enemies feel like they are underwhelming and you can just button mash. And that is a shame, because you waited to 30 minutes to fight them.

The final 5% of the time, you are in a crammed location, fighting 6 enemies, and cannot meaningfully land attacks and see what is happening at the same time because of the camera. Additionally, many attacks are simply undodgable and will stagger you even when blocking. This means that with just 3-4 enemies, you can sometimes find yourself taking many big AoE hits in succession with no counterplay and that often just oneshots your squishier characters. This happens more often than it should and it is not like it can be overcome by skill, the timing just works out that way and it becomes a bad experience.

It honestly feels like they wanted to make a 60-hr long movie catered toward people that will only ever play on easy difficulty. Because the harder difficulties just don’t feel like they were ever thoughtfully tested or balanced. It’s a lot worse than any of FF I’ve played and it’s a shame because this remake has been their only priority for 10 years. 

Let’s hope they can remember how to make games that FEEL good, not just look good.

[h1]Recommended – 8.5/10[/h1]

[b]A gorgeous, fun, but slightly uneven remake with incredible highs.[/b]

[h2]The Good[/h2]
[b]• Stunning graphics[/b] in both cutscenes and gameplay.
[b]• Phenomenal soundtrack[/b] with unique themes for every area.
[b]• Combat is fluid and rewarding[/b], with great materia and weapon synergy.
[b]• Characters are expressive, well‑acted, and memorable.[/b]
[b]• INTERmission DLC gameplay is fast, stylish, and challenging.[/b]

[h2]The Mixed[/h2]
• Difficulty curve is slow early on; real challenge arrives late.
• Some characters are locked out for long stretches despite having deep kits.
• Limited weapon variety and no transmog/customization options.
• Status effects could use better in‑game explanations.

[h2]The Not‑So‑Good[/h2]
• Platforming and gimmick sections (motorcycle, crane puzzles) feel like padding.
• DLC dialogue is pretty [spoiler]cringe[/spoiler] compared to the main game.

[hr][/hr]

[b]Overall:[/b]
If you love stylish combat, top‑tier music, and beautiful worldbuilding, this remake delivers. It’s not perfect, but the highs are absolutely worth the journey—especially if you enjoy mastering combat systems.

FF7 Remake is a great game largely owing to the brilliantly crafted world, interesting characters and peak soundtrack.

It's rare for me to say that the gameplay is probably the worst part of a game, but I do feel that's the case here. I want to be fair, I appreciate the unique blend of action and turn-based combat and I only single it out because everything else is so good. When it works, it works and I do think there is a learning curve to it, but still I found it often lacking. The combat struggles with flow, dodging feels really awkward and fighting multiple enemies at once is a pain. Outside of combat, I found the puzzles pretty boring and traversal frustratingly slow at times. There are also various gameplay systems; I think Materia are pretty cool. Not perfect, but interesting to play around with. I like the unique weapon abilities but, on the other hand, the weapon upgrade system is just a bit annoying with how many times you have to do it. There is a auto-upgrade option, thankfully.

On to all the other positives. As I said the characters are great and I was super invested in the story. What I appreciated was how well they bounced off each other and could be quite funny. The voice acting and direction is good almost all the time. Midgard is a really cool and 'believable' setting in the sense that you get a good idea for how this world works and the troubles of the people in it. The soundtrack is massive and varied, and all the combat music compliments the action well.

As an aside, the minigames are kinda fun and the Intergrade content is good because the game give you a nuclear bomb in the form of a character and that makes the combat a lot more fun.

Overall, I definitely recommend for JRPG fans, just keep in mind you're in for a long ride with two more games after this one.

Final Fantasy VII Remake is one of those games that had an almost impossible job. The original Final Fantasy VII is regarded as one of the most important RPGs ever made, and for many players it is tied to a huge amount of nostalgia. Remaking it was always going to be risky. Square Enix could have simply updated the graphics and modernised the combat, but instead they chose to completely rethink how the story is told. Thankfully, for the most part, it works brilliantly.

The first thing that stands out is Midgar itself. The original game gave us a relatively limited view of the city, but Remake turns it into a huge, atmospheric place that feels alive. The slums, markets, factories and towering plate all have their own character. Walking around Midgar is often as enjoyable as the actual missions because there is so much environmental detail to take in.

The combat is probably the biggest improvement. The original's turn-based system has been replaced with a fast-paced hybrid that combines real-time action with traditional RPG mechanics. You can switch between characters, use abilities, spells and items, and still pause the action to make tactical decisions. It sounds like it shouldn't work as well as it does, but it quickly becomes second nature. Each character also feels genuinely different to play. Cloud is powerful and versatile, Barret is great at keeping his distance, Tifa is incredibly fast, and Aerith brings a completely different approach.

The characters are another major strength. Cloud, in particular, is much more developed than he was at this point in the original. His awkward personality and occasional deadpan humour make him far more likeable. Tifa and Aerith are also given considerably more time to develop, and their relationships with Cloud feel believable rather than simply being there to move the plot forward.

However, the game isn't perfect. Because Square Enix has expanded what was originally only part of the overall story into a full-leng…

The only major downside to the combat is the AI of party members when you're not actively controlling them as they tend to not contribute as much as they should. The expansion of midgar's story section from a maybe 5 hour section to 40+ hours is a mixed bag. I dislike the some of the pacing, characterization/buildup of Sephiroth, and most stuff to do with the whispers but I like the expansion of other characters and how moments get expanded into a much greater spectacle. Some of the new sections are good and some feel like padding. Even some of the padding I don't mind as it gave more opportunities to enjoy the combat. The voice acting is also excellent and perfectly fits the characters. The remixed soundtrack is good as well, though some songs sounded better in the original. Anyways it's a good game and I look forward to part 3.

Went in with big expectations and came out kinda deflated. The game is incredibly padded, so much of it is just filler stretched out to fill time.

The story didn't really grip me, confused me more than anything. Finished it and still have no idea what happened overall. There's no answer to the "why?". And Sephiroth shows up every five minutes, which feels like fan-service at this point, not actual storytelling.

The combat is a mess, at conflict with its own systems. It's supposed to be action but I'm constantly stuck in the command menu. And the enemies CC you nonstop, you get a dodge but can't actually dodge most attacks anyway. Most bosses have scripted sequences where the stagger bar resets on you. I'd take FFXV's combat over this, at least that one felt like it was actually designed around something.

Here's the thing though, I actually like JRPGs. If the story had gripped me I probably wouldn't even care about the combat. But it didn't, so I'm left with all the flaws and nothing carrying me through them. I genuinely don't get how this gets praised as much as it does. Those are some very big flaws to wave away.

It's my first time playing FF7 thoroughly cuz I've never played the original FF7 till the end. But all I can say is the overall gameplay really is genius in the making. It's like you can choose turn-based while still in action or something like that... it's kinda hard to explain, but I really loved it. And yeah, I think it's safe to say the soundtrack is just pure fire till the end, even though I kinda see many old fans still prefer some of the OST from the original FF7. But well, at least for me, it's actually very good. And yeah, the quality or QoL upgrade from the original to the Remake is just pure gold. Absolutely gorgeous, and I really recommend trying this game as someone who's new to this specific remake of the 7th installment in the series.

Final Fantasy VII Remake is a masterclass in how to ruin a classic with bloat, artificial friction, and garbage design. What should have been an epic journey is instead a deeply frustrating slog filled with linear hallways, mind-numbing padding, and tedious side quests that do nothing but waste your time.
The combat system is completely built like trash. It tries to blend action and menus but fails miserably at both, resulting in an over-engineered nightmare. Throughout the entire game, you are constantly fighting terrible camera tracking, input lag, and clunky targeting. Worse, the developers obsessed over heavily scripted boss fights bogged down by invisible shield gimmicks, arbitrary phase shifts, and hidden weaknesses that completely ignore actual tactical skill. It turns what should be an exciting battle into a miserable hostage situation.
Square Enix has fallen so incredibly far from their peak. If you want to remember when this company actually knew how to design a masterpiece with flawless pacing, intuitive mechanics, and a truly brilliant battle system, go play Final Fantasy X. This remake is a bloated, artificial, poorly paced disaster. Save your sanity and avoid it.

Also there are pacing issues, Like forcing you to just walk for no reason whatsoever, that one actually happens a lot.
I'm actually at odds with this, cause there are parts that i like, quite a lot in fact.
This game is a clear case where we are lacking the neutral grade for a game Which would be far more in line with my grade than a simple downvote.

Normally I would only play the game once but since the game is so short that I still want more out of it by continuing in hard mode(at least until half way through). Might be because it is a linear game experience without much exploration available. So the second play through still feel ok. Intergrade DLC is fun and you get to experience something new with Yuffie.
